newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks rise for 6th day, hit new record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks rise for 6th day, hit new record.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose in light trade for the sixth consecutive session to a record high on sunny growth prospects for the coming year, traders said.
The sustained rise "is due to the positive outlook for 1997 and a number of investors taking positions on that," said one trader.
Ministers have said economic growth would reach four percent in 1997 and top six percent from 1998 onward.
The market's leading .IBC index gained 0.5 percent to close at 6,476.15 points as 17 shares rose, 11 fell and six closed flat, according to preliminary figures from the bourse.
Volume was boosted to 51 million shares, worth 3.2 billion bolivars ($6.8 million), with more than 35 million shares cross-traded in real estate fund Fondo de Valores Inmobilarios.

Among the day's other leading trades, 10 million Corimon Type B shares changed hands, with the stock closing up 0.35 bolivars at 9.00. Utility Electricidad de Caracas meanwhile slipped 1.50 bolivars to end at 548.50, while telephone company CANTV moved ahead 10.25 bolivars to close at 1840.25 bolivars
